name: Chapter 7: Redox Reactions
description: Classical and electronic redox, oxidation number rules, types of redox reactions, balancing by two methods, redox titrations and electrode potentials

cards.term: Everyday processes that are redox?
cards.definition: Burning fuels, extraction of reactive metals, making caustic soda, batteries, corrosion

cards.term: Environmental issues linked to redox (NCERT)?
cards.definition: Hydrogen economy (liquid H₂ as fuel) and the ozone hole

cards.term: Original meaning of oxidation?
cards.definition: Addition of oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO; S + O₂ → SO₂

cards.text: Classical oxidation: addition of {{c1::oxygen/electronegative element}} or removal of {{c2::hydrogen/electropositive element}}.
Classical reduction: removal of {{c1::oxygen/electronegative element}} or addition of {{c2::hydrogen/electropositive element}}.

cards.term: Why is 2H₂S + O₂ → 2S + 2H₂O an oxidation of H₂S?
cards.definition: Removal of hydrogen from H₂S

cards.term: Why is K₄[Fe(CN)₆] → K₃[Fe(CN)₆] (with H₂O₂) an oxidation?
cards.definition: Removal of the electropositive element potassium

cards.term: Classify: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂; 2FeCl₃ + H₂ → 2FeCl₂ + 2HCl; C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆.
cards.definition: All reductions: removal of O; removal of Cl; addition of H

cards.term: 2HgCl₂ + SnCl₂ → Hg₂Cl₂ + SnCl₄: what is oxidised and reduced?
cards.definition: HgCl₂ reduced (Hg added); SnCl₂ oxidised (Cl added)

cards.term: Why the word "redox"?
cards.definition: Oxidation and reduction always occur together

cards.term: Problem 7.1: oxidised/reduced in H₂S + Cl₂ → 2HCl + S; 3Fe₃O₄ + 8Al → 9Fe + 4Al₂O₃; 2Na + H₂ → 2NaH?
cards.definition:
(i) H₂S oxidised, Cl₂ reduced.
(ii) Al oxidised, Fe₃O₄ reduced.
(iii) Na oxidised, H₂ reduced.

cards.text: Oxidation = {{c1::loss}} of electrons; reduction = {{c2::gain}} of electrons; oxidising agent = electron {{c3::acceptor}}; reducing agent = electron {{c4::donor}}.

cards.term: Mnemonic for electron transfer? (intuition)
cards.definition: "OIL RIG": Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain

cards.term: What is a half reaction?
cards.definition: One step showing only loss or gain of electrons, e.g. 2Na → 2Na⁺ + 2e⁻

cards.term: In 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl, which is the reducing agent?
cards.definition: Na (it donates electrons and is itself oxidised)

cards.term: Why is 2Na + H₂ → 2NaH redox? (Problem 7.2)
cards.definition: NaH is Na⁺H⁻: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻ (oxidised); H₂ + 2e⁻ → 2H⁻ (reduced)

cards.term: Zn strip in Cu(NO₃)₂ solution: observations?
cards.definition: Reddish copper coats the zinc; blue colour disappears

cards.term: Test for Zn²⁺ formed in that reaction?
cards.definition: Pass H₂S in ammoniacal solution: white ZnS

cards.term: Cu strip in ZnSO₄: what happens?
cards.definition: No reaction: not even CuS (a very sensitive test) forms; equilibrium greatly favours Zn²⁺ + Cu

cards.term: Cu in AgNO₃ solution?
cards.definition: Solution turns blue (Cu²⁺); silver deposits: Cu + 2Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + 2Ag

cards.term: Co in NiSO₄: which side is favoured?
cards.definition: Neither: both Ni²⁺ and Co²⁺ present at moderate concentrations

cards.term: Electron-releasing order of Zn, Cu, Ag?
cards.definition: Zn > Cu > Ag

cards.term: What does electron competition lead to?
cards.definition: The activity (electrochemical) series and galvanic cells

cards.term: Why is H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O called redox though no ions form?
cards.definition: Electrons shift partially from H to O; oxidation number treats it as complete transfer (book-keeping)

cards.term: Define oxidation number.
cards.definition: Charge an atom would have if every bonding pair belonged entirely to the more electronegative atom

cards.text: Rules: free elements have O.N. {{c1::0}}; a monatomic ion has O.N. = its {{c2::charge}}; alkali metals {{c3::+1}}, alkaline earths {{c4::+2}}, Al {{c5::+3}} in compounds.

cards.term: Oxidation number of oxygen: usual and exceptions?
cards.definition: Usually −2; peroxides −1; superoxides −½; OF₂ +2; O₂F₂ +1

cards.term: Oxidation number of hydrogen: usual and exception?
cards.definition: +1; −1 in binary metal hydrides (LiH, NaH, CaH₂)

cards.term: Oxidation number of halogens?
cards.definition: F always −1; Cl, Br, I are −1 as halides but positive with oxygen (oxoacids)

cards.term: Sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound and an ion?
cards.definition: Zero in a compound; equal to the ion charge in a polyatomic ion

cards.term: Highest oxidation number of a representative element?
cards.definition: Group number (groups 1, 2); group number − 10 for groups 13–17

cards.term: O.N. of Mn in K₂MnO₄ and of B in NaBH₄?
cards.definition: Mn +6; B +3 (H is −1)

cards.term: O.N. of O in CaO₂ and of S in H₂S₂O₇?
cards.definition: O −1 (peroxide); S +6

cards.term: What is Stock notation?
cards.definition: Roman numeral for the metal’s O.N. in brackets: Au(I)Cl, Au(III)Cl₃, Sn(II)Cl₂, Sn(IV)Cl₄ (Alfred Stock)

cards.term: Stock notation for HAuCl₄, Tl₂O, Fe₂O₃, CuI, MnO₂? (Problem 7.3)
cards.definition: HAu(III)Cl₄, Tl₂(I)O, Fe₂(III)O₃, Cu(I)I, Mn(IV)O₂

cards.text: In terms of O.N.: oxidation = {{c1::increase}} in O.N.; reduction = {{c2::decrease}} in O.N.; an oxidant {{c3::increases}} another element’s O.N.

cards.term: 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂: oxidant and reductant? (Problem 7.4)
cards.definition: Cu(+1) → 0 reduced; S(−2) → +4 oxidised. Cu(I) is the oxidant; S of Cu₂S is the reductant.

cards.term: Fractional oxidation numbers: examples?
cards.definition: C₃O₂: 4/3; Br₃O₈: 16/3; S₄O₆²⁻: 2.5

cards.term: What does a fractional O.N. really mean?
cards.definition: An average: atoms are in different whole-number states (e.g. S₄O₆²⁻ has S at +5, 0, 0, +5)

cards.term: Real oxidation states in C₃O₂ and Br₃O₈?
Mixed oxides with fractional average O.N.?
cards.definition: Fe₃O₄, Mn₃O₄, Pb₃O₄

cards.term: O.N. of I in KI₃ and of Fe in Fe₃O₄? (Ex 7.2)
cards.definition: I: −1/3 (really I⁻·I₂). Fe: +8/3 (Fe²⁺ + 2Fe³⁺).

cards.term: O.N. of S in H₂SO₅ by formula vs by structure? (Ex 7.5)
cards.definition: Formula gives +8 (impossible); structure has a peroxide O–O, so S is +6

cards.term: Four types of redox reactions
cards.definition: Combination: C + O₂ → CO₂; 3Mg + N₂ → Mg₃N₂; Decomposition: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂; Metal displacement: CuSO₄ + Zn → Cu + ZnSO₄; Non-metal displacement: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂; Disproportionation: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂

Example?

CombinationC + O₂ → CO₂; 3Mg + N₂ → Mg₃N₂
Decomposition2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂

Disproportionation2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂

cards.term: When is a combination reaction redox?
cards.definition: When A or B (or both) is an element

cards.term: Is every decomposition a redox reaction?
cards.definition: No: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ has no O.N. change

cards.term: Metal displacement reactions in metallurgy?
cards.definition: V₂O₅ + 5Ca → 2V + 5CaO; TiCl₄ + 2Mg → Ti + 2MgCl₂; Cr₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Cr

cards.term: Which metals displace H₂ from cold water?
cards.definition: All alkali metals and Ca, Sr, Ba

cards.term: Which metals need steam to give H₂?
cards.definition: Mg and Fe

cards.term: Correction: NCERT writes 2Fe + 3H₂O → Fe₂O₃ + 3H₂. What does iron actually give with steam?
cards.definition: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂ (magnetic oxide)

cards.term: Metals that don’t react with steam but displace H₂ from acids?
cards.definition: Cadmium and tin

cards.term: Rate of H₂ evolution with HCl: Mg, Zn, Fe?
cards.definition: Mg fastest, Fe slowest

cards.term: Metals that don’t react even with HCl?
cards.definition: Ag and Au (occur native)

cards.term: Oxidising power order of halogens?
cards.definition: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂

cards.term: What does F₂ do with water?
cards.definition: Displaces oxygen: 2H₂O + 2F₂ → 4HF + O₂

cards.term: Basis of the "layer test" for Br⁻ and I⁻?
cards.definition: Cl₂ displaces Br₂/I₂, which dissolve in CCl₄ with characteristic colour

cards.term: Can Br₂ displace I⁻?
cards.definition: Yes: Br₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Br⁻ + I₂

cards.term: How is F₂ obtained from F⁻?
cards.definition: Only by electrolysis: no chemical oxidant is stronger than F₂

cards.term: Define disproportionation.
cards.definition: An element in one oxidation state is simultaneously oxidised and reduced

cards.term: Requirement for a species to disproportionate?
cards.definition: Element must have at least three oxidation states and be in an intermediate one

cards.term: Disproportionation of P₄, S₈, Cl₂ in alkali?
cards.definition: P₄ → PH₃ (−3) + H₂PO₂⁻ (+1); S₈ → S²⁻ (−2) + S₂O₃²⁻ (+2); Cl₂ → Cl⁻ (−1) + ClO⁻ (+1)

cards.term: Everyday use of Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O?
cards.definition: Household bleach (ClO⁻ oxidises coloured stains)

cards.term: Why does fluorine not disproportionate?
cards.definition: Most electronegative: it cannot show positive oxidation states (F₂ + OH⁻ gives F⁻ + OF₂)

cards.term: Which of ClO⁻, ClO₂⁻, ClO₃⁻, ClO₄⁻ won’t disproportionate? (Problem 7.5)
cards.definition: ClO₄⁻: Cl is already +7 (highest)

cards.term: Classify N₂ + O₂ → 2NO; 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂; NaH + H₂O → NaOH + H₂; 2NO₂ + 2OH⁻ → NO₂⁻ + NO₃⁻ + H₂O. (Problem 7.6)
cards.definition: Combination; decomposition; displacement; disproportionation

cards.term: Why does Pb₃O₄ give Cl₂ with HCl but PbO₂ with HNO₃? (Problem 7.7)
cards.definition: Pb₃O₄ = 2PbO + PbO₂. PbO₂ (+4) oxidises Cl⁻ to Cl₂; HNO₃ is itself an oxidant, so PbO₂ stays unreacted.

cards.text: Oxidation number method: assign O.N.s → equalise {{c1::increase and decrease}} → balance charge with {{c2::H⁺ (acid) or OH⁻ (base)}} → balance H with {{c3::H₂O}} → check O.

cards.term: Balanced: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + SO₃²⁻ in acid → Cr³⁺ + SO₄²⁻. (Problem 7.8)
cards.definition: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3SO₃²⁻ + 8H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3SO₄²⁻ + 4H₂O

cards.term: Balanced: MnO₄⁻ + Br⁻ in base → MnO₂ + BrO₃⁻. (Problem 7.9)
cards.definition: 2MnO₄⁻ + Br⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + BrO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻

cards.term: Dichromate–ferrous balancing
cards.definition: 6Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ → 6Fe³⁺ + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Half-reaction method

Balance Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ → Fe³⁺ + Cr³⁺ (acid).

Balance each half, then equalise electrons.
  1. ?
  2. Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ (× 6)
  3. Add: 6Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ → 6Fe³⁺ + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Half-reaction method

Balance Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ → Fe³⁺ + Cr³⁺ (acid).

Balance each half, then equalise electrons.
  1. Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O
  2. Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ (× 6)
  3. Add: 6Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ → 6Fe³⁺ + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O

cards.term: Half-reaction method: how to handle basic medium?
cards.definition: Balance as in acid, then add OH⁻ equal to H⁺ on both sides and combine into H₂O

cards.term: Balanced: MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ in base → MnO₂ + I₂. (Problem 7.10)
cards.definition: 2MnO₄⁻ + 6I⁻ + 4H₂O → 2MnO₂ + 3I₂ + 8OH⁻

cards.term: Electrons gained by MnO₄⁻ in acid, neutral/weakly basic, strongly basic? (JEE)
cards.definition: Acid → Mn²⁺: 5; neutral → MnO₂: 3; strong base → MnO₄²⁻: 1

cards.term: Trap: sanity check while balancing by O.N.?
cards.definition: If two things are reduced and nothing oxidised, a formula or O.N. is wrong

cards.term: Why is KMnO₄ a self-indicator?
cards.definition: Intensely purple: the first lasting pink tinge marks the end point (at ~10⁻⁶ M MnO₄⁻)

cards.term: Indicator for dichromate titrations?
cards.definition: Diphenylamine: oxidised after the equivalence point to intense blue

cards.term: What is the equivalence point?
cards.definition: Where oxidant and reductant are equal in mole stoichiometry

cards.term: Iodometric reactions with Cu²⁺?
cards.definition: 2Cu²⁺ + 4I⁻ → Cu₂I₂ + I₂; then I₂ + 2S₂O₃²⁻ → 2I⁻ + S₄O₆²⁻

cards.term: End point in iodometry?
cards.definition: Starch gives intense blue with I₂; colour vanishes when thiosulphate consumes all I₂

cards.term: How does iodine stay in solution though insoluble in water?
cards.definition: As KI₃ in KI solution

cards.term: Modern view of oxidation and reduction (limitation of O.N.)?
cards.definition: Oxidation = decrease in electron density; reduction = increase

cards.term: Zn rod in CuSO₄: how is electron transfer made indirect?
cards.definition: Separate Zn|ZnSO₄ and Cu|CuSO₄ in two beakers, link by a wire and a salt bridge

cards.term: Define a redox couple and its notation.
cards.definition: Oxidised and reduced forms of a species in a half reaction, written oxidised/reduced: Zn²⁺/Zn, Cu²⁺/Cu

cards.term: What is a salt bridge made of, and its job?
cards.definition: U-tube of KCl or NH₄NO₃ set in agar-agar jelly; electrical contact without mixing

cards.term: Figure 7.3 · Daniell cell
Direction of electron flow vs current in a Daniell cell?
cards.definition: Electrons: Zn → Cu through the wire; current flows the opposite way

cards.term: Define standard electrode potential.
cards.definition: Electrode potential with all species at unit concentration (gases 1 atm) and 298 K

cards.term: Reference electrode and its E°?
cards.definition: Standard hydrogen electrode: E° = 0.00 V

cards.term: Meaning of negative vs positive E°?
cards.definition: Negative: stronger reducing agent than H⁺/H₂. Positive: weaker reducing agent (stronger oxidant).

cards.term: Strongest oxidant and strongest reductant in Table 7.1?
cards.definition: Oxidant: F₂ (+2.87 V). Reductant: Li (−3.05 V).

cards.term: E° of Cu²⁺/Cu and Zn²⁺/Zn?
cards.definition: +0.34 V and −0.76 V

cards.term: Why does Zn displace Cu²⁺ but not the reverse? (intuition)
cards.definition: Zn²⁺/Zn has a more negative E°: zinc gives up electrons more readily, like water flowing downhill

cards.term: Mnemonic for reading the E° table? (intuition)
cards.definition: "Top-left grabs, bottom-right gives": high E° oxidised forms are strong oxidants; low E° reduced forms are strong reductants

cards.term: Evolving definitions of oxidation
cards.definition: Classical: Add O / electronegative element; remove H / electropositive; Electronic: Loss of electrons; Oxidation number: Increase in O.N.; Modern: Decrease in electron density
